Price is a quality signal, not a barrier: 'The price doesn't really shock me, to be honest. It's something that I would expect'

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, it's more like a trying out thing, so how can I fit [kettlebells] into my current life and current schedule, and discover if it's something for me, and maybe later on, yeah, I would be open to do like a full package thing, but it's not really what I'm looking for right now.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it rather than rebutting. He had already surfaced the mismatch himself a minute earlier ('is it that you're really looking for full guidance, or are you maybe looking for just something to try out first') and had pre-framed the price at 'at least like in the four figures' without naming $6,000. He then offered two paths and let the prospect pick the lower one.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah. The price doesn't really shock me, to be honest. It's something that I would expect from a schedule like it. But yeah, I think my question is just a bit different maybe than what you're offering. So yeah, if that is what it is then.
objections.rep_response: Asked him to specify what he actually wanted — 'like just lay it out to me. Like what are the main things that you feel like that is what I would need?' — which produced a precise description of a hybrid programming review the offer does not provide.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, maybe if you can just send me what it actually all means, then I could just have a look at it.
objections.rep_response: Sent a link on WhatsApp immediately, confirmed the phone number aloud, and made no attempt to close on the $2,000/$200 tier. Set an expectation of seeing the prospect's introduction post 'on Monday or Tuesday' and a check-in call in one to two months.

evidence: The $6,000 six-month one-to-one offer was never presented. The rep deliberately routed away from it after establishing the prospect wanted an adjunct rather than a transformation, describing it only as 'an investment at least like in the four figures'.
What was presented and priced was a separate lower tier at '$2,000 a year or $200 a month' — referred to internally as Primal University but never named on this call.

No payment was taken and no verbal agreement was given. The rep said 'Perfect. Let's get you started with that' and the prospect immediately asked 'What do you mean with getting started?', then deferred: 'maybe if you can just send me what it actually all means, then I could just have a look at it.'
A WhatsApp link was sent live during the call, but as information to review rather than against an agreement, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link close rule does not apply.
Counter-evidence toward a close: 'Sounds interesting', 'I'll take a look at it over the weekend', and no price resistance at any point.
Counter-evidence against: the prospect never said yes, and the specific thing he asked for — a review of his existing gym programme with kettlebell days blended in — is not what he was sent.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to review the WhatsApp link over the weekend and post an introduction in the community on Monday or Tuesday; rep to schedule a check-in one to two months out to revisit the one-to-one.

notable.note: The only call in this batch where the $6,000 offer was deliberately not presented. The rep diagnosed the scope mismatch early and honestly and routed the prospect to a $2,000/year or $200/month tier that appears nowhere in the stated offer structure — and the two figures do not reconcile, since twelve months at $200 is $2,400. Two consequences for the audit: this call must not sit in the $6,000 close-rate denominator, and the existence of a second priced tier changes what 'the offer' means corpus-wide. Clinically, the prospect disclosed an unhealed meniscus tear and knee pain; the rep did screen for injuries, and the prospect's physiotherapist had specifically recommended kettlebell lunges, but nobody asked whether the physio had cleared an unsupervised self-directed programme, which is what he was then sold. The rep also read the prospect's full mobile number aloud on the recording.
